newsitem.title: UK: Virgin's Branson is UK top headline grabber.
newsitem.headline: Virgin's Branson is UK top headline grabber.

text.p: Richard Branson, flamboyant founder and head of Britain's Virgin Group, is the UK's top headline grabber -- outranking even Princess Diana, according to a report released on Monday.

The 46-year-old Branson works harder at grabbing headlines than any other British celebrity, even willing to turn his own failures into media events, Durrants Press Cuttings, a newspaper clipping service, said in quarterly report.

"The Princess of Wales is an on-going headline grabber of the highest order, but we don't believe she has put as much effort into securing media interest as Mr Branson," said Tony Law, managing director of Durrants.

Undaunted by the failure of his attempt to make a round-the-world balloon flight -- with a forced landing in Algeria less than 24 hours after taking off from Morocco -- Branson later turned up at the launches of two rival balloonists.

Then, unfazed by the departure of BBC Radio 1 disc jockey Chris Evans for New York, Branson booked a flight on the Concorde and jetted off in an attempt to sign him on to Virgin Radio's evening slot, Durrants said.

Branson, whose Virgin Group ranges from Virgin Atlantic Airways to radio stations, music stores, and cola and vodka brands, tops a list of UK headline grabbers including Princess Diana, Labour leader Tony Blair, the Duchess of York and the pop group the Spice Girls.

Durrant said he believes that future quarterly results of his media survey will prominently feature Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams, Referendum Party founder Sir James Goldsmith and composer Lord Andrew Lloyd Webber.
